headline: Record revenue, but the operating ratio worsened

drivers.explanation: Volume rose 3% y/y and higher fuel surcharges contributed eight points of the revenue growth.
Release notes productivity gains but rising fuel costs and merger-related expenses; adjusted operating ratio was 65.4%, 210 bps higher than adjusted prior-year quarter.
Management cites a tighter trucking market and continued network productivity as supporting rail demand.

summary_short: Norfolk Southern posted record Q3 revenue of $3.5B (+14% y/y) and diluted EPS of $3.37 (+7%); adjusted EPS was $3.62 (+10%).
summary_long: Revenue growth came from 3% higher volume and fuel surcharges worth eight points. Income from railway operations rose 5% to $1.15B, but the operating ratio rose to 67.4% from 64.6% (adjusted 65.4%, up 210 bps). Results include merger-related expenses and effects of the Eastern Ohio incident. The release gives no numeric guidance.
confidence_notes: Adjusted figures exclude merger-related expenses and Eastern Ohio incident effects (and restructuring in 2025); they are company-defined non-GAAP measures. Revenue delta is the release's rounded +14%.
